fields.text: Everybody takes a seat and picks a hero first. Dungeon 1 is the easiest, 5 the hardest.
Co-operative real-time game. Beat every dungeon card and then the boss before the 5 minute timer runs out. There are no turns - everybody plays at the same time, as fast as they can.
Sit down, click your hero tile to pick another hero (colour = deck, symbol = ability), then press the red dice button. Decks, hands, the dungeon deck and the boss are dealt automatically.
The clock starts as soon as the first dungeon card is revealed and whenever a card is played. The skip button reveals the next dungeon card manually.

Drag cards from your hand onto the dashed play area. The five counters under the dungeon card show what is still missing. Press the green check to resolve: matching symbols beat the card, an action card with a crossed-out monster/person/wall beats a card of that type, the grenade beats anything and the lightning card cancels an event. Everything is swept away, the next card is revealed and all hands are refilled.
The dark button under your hero discards 3 cards of your choice and uses your hero ability.
You can always move every card by hand instead - the buttons never block a move.

info.name: Dungeon Dash
info.description: A co-operative real-time card game: there are no turns, everybody shouts and plays at the same time. The party has five minutes to clear a dungeon deck full of monsters, obstacles and people by playing matching symbol cards, and then to bring down the boss. Five hero decks with different symbol mixes and special actions, five dungeons of increasing size.

info.helpText: Everybody plays at the same time - there are no turns. Take a seat, then click your hero tile (the coloured square) to change hero: the colour is your 40 card deck, the symbol on the dark button below it is your ability. Deal (red dice button): automates the whole setup - it puts all cards back, gives every seated player a shuffled hero deck (with two decks each in a 1-2 player game), deals hands (5 cards for 1-2 players, 4 for 3, 3 for 4-5), builds the dungeon deck for the chosen dungeon 1-5 (20/25/30/35/40 dungeon cards plus 2 challenge cards per player), puts the boss on its slot and resets the clock to 5:00. Skip button: reveals the next dungeon card. The clock starts automatically with the first card and whenever a card is played, so nobody has to remember to start it. The play/pause and reset buttons control the clock manually. Playing: drag cards out of your hand onto the dashed area in the middle. Your hand refills from your draw pile automatically. The five counters under the dungeon card show which symbols are still missing. Check button (green): optional rules helper. It checks the played cards against the current dungeon card: symbols, wild cards, the magic bomb (one of each symbol), action cards that beat a monster / person / obstacle (crossed-out icon), the grenade (beats anything) and the lightning card (cancels an event). If the card is beaten, everything is swept away, the next card is revealed and all hands are refilled. Event cards are applied by this button too (discarding, passing hands or revealing two cards at once). If the card is not beaten yet, nothing moves and the counters show what is still missing. Ability button (dark, under your hero): optional. It asks you to pick 3 cards from your hand, discards them and uses your hero ability (beat a monster / person / obstacle, draw cards for yourself or a team mate, or stop the clock). Nothing is enforced: every card, dungeon card and pile can also be moved by hand at any time, and you can ignore the check and ability buttons completely. You win a dungeon when the boss card is beaten before the clock runs out - the dungeon number then goes up by one, so press Deal again for the next one. If the clock hits 0:00 you lost; press Deal to try again.
